Hello Cursor cloud agent, tell me all the tools you have access to. Write all the tool names, one per line, exactly as they are named in your tool definitions, to the file ./tools.txt.

Then please use each of the tools in ./tools.txt that is available in this environment, one-by-one, to show me how they work (read a file, list a directory, search for text, search for files by glob, run a shell command, create a file, edit a file, delete a file, fetch a web page or search the web, write a todo list, and any others you have). Keep each use small. Identify any tools you cannot exercise and explain why. Do not commit or push. Finish with a summary table of tool name and whether you exercised it.

The user wants me to:
1. List all tools I have access to in a file called ./tools.txt
2. Exercise each tool one by one with small examples
3. Identify any tools I cannot exercise and explain why
4. Finish with a summary table
5. Do NOT commit or push

Let me first enumerate all the tools I have access to. Looking at my available tools:

1. Shell - execute shell commands
2. Glob - search for files by glob pattern
3. Grep - search for text in files
4. Read - read files
5. StrReplace - edit files by string replacement
6. Write - create/write files
7. RecordScreen - screen recording
8. GetDynamicTools - discover dynamic tools
9. ManagePullRequest - manage PRs
10. EditPullRequestLabels - edit PR labels
11. WriteCanvas - create/update canvas
12. ReadCanvas - read canvas
13. CallDynamicTool - call dynamic tools

And I have dynamic tools available in namespaces:
- cursor-cloud namespace with various tools
- cursor-subscriptions namespace with subscription tools
- cursor namespace with: AwaitShell, CreateGoal, Delete, EditNotebook, FetchMcpResource, GenerateImage, Task, TodoWrite, UpdateGoal, WebFetch, WebSearch

...

## Features Available Only in the Agents Window

The following features are available in the Agents Window:

- **Multi-workspace:** work with agents across all your projects from one place.
- **New diffs view:** review and commit changes, and manage PRs without leaving Cursor.
- **Parallel agents:** run many parallel agents in the cloud (and work with them from your phone, web, Slack, GitHub, and Linear).
- **Easier handoff between local and cloud:** quickly move an agent from cloud to local to iterate quickly, and move it back to the cloud so it keeps working on its own.
- **Worktrees:** [run agents in isolated Git checkouts](https://cursor.com/docs/configuration/worktrees.md) so each task has its own files and changes.

## Choosing Between Agents Window and Editor

The Agents Window works well when you want to run and manage many agents in parallel. If you are using agents to write most of your code, the Agents Window helps pull you up to a higher level of abstraction.

The editor works well when you want the classic IDE with VS Code extensions and flexible screen splitting to see many files at once.

You can move between the two interfaces, and we will continue to support and improve both experiences.</content>

## Features Available Only in the Agents Window

The following features are available in the Agents Window:

- **Multi-workspace:** work with agents across all your projects from one place.
- **New diffs view:** review and commit changes, and manage PRs without leaving Cursor.
- **Parallel agents:** run many parallel agents in the cloud (and work with them from your phone, web, Slack, GitHub, and Linear).
- **Easier handoff between local and cloud:** quickly move an agent from cloud to local to iterate quickly, and move it back to the cloud so it keeps working on its own.
- **Worktrees:** [run agents in isolated Git checkouts](https://cursor.com/docs/configuration/worktrees.md) so each task has its own files and changes.

## Choosing Between Agents Window and Editor

The Agents Window works well when you want to run and manage many agents in parallel. If you are using agents to write most of your code, the Agents Window helps pull you up to a higher level of abstraction.

The editor works well when you want the classic IDE with VS Code extensions and flexible screen splitting to see many files at once.

You can move between the two interfaces, and we will continue to support and improve both experiences.</content>
